nh_big_wall_2.blurb: The Big Wall is the tallest stretch of Cannon Cliff, a roughly 1,000-foot face of granite above Franconia Notch. Its eleven climbs are long, serious days of seven to eleven pitches, mostly trad and alpine in style, plus a few aid lines that make it the only true big-wall aid climbing in the state. Free grades run from the 5.7 range through the 5.10s, with the bulk at 5.11 and a couple at 5.12. This is a place for experienced parties: expect a committed approach on the Moby Grape trail, an early start, and weather that can turn quickly.
nh_big_wall_2.approach: Follow the Moby Grape trail up toward the cliff, then angle left to reach the Big Wall.

nh_6_standard_route_area.blurb: Standard Route Area is a winter ice venue on Frankenstein Cliff in Crawford Notch, a short walk from the road. Of its eleven climbs, ten are water ice, mostly WI3 with a handful at WI4, and one is a mixed line around M5. Routes are typically one or two pitches, which suits parties stepping up to multi-pitch ice. The area is one of the notch's best-known and is regularly crowded, so expect to share the flows and watch for ice falling from parties above.

nh_el_wall.blurb: El Wall is a sport crag within Jackson Crag, set on the hillside above Jackson in the Bartlett area. All eleven climbs are bolted, between about 35 and 90 feet tall. The spread leans hard: a pair of 5.8s and a 5.10, then five 5.11s, two 5.12s and a 5.13 project. Permanent draws hang on some lines, and a stick clip is handy because the ground at the base is blocky. A good pick for climbers working 5.11 who want a quiet, modest-sized wall, though not a beginner venue.

nh_lantern_boulder.blurb: Lantern Boulder is a single block of problems tucked beside Norris Brook at the edge of the forest in Exeter's Town Forest South bouldering zone. It holds eleven problems with a wide range: four at V0, a few easy to moderate lines, then a run of hard ones from V5 up to V9, including the area's well-regarded Green Lantern. The boulder is reached quickly from the Commerce Way entrance, about 200 yards along the brook trail, with the rock across the water. Trails in the surrounding woods are confusing and bugs can be harsh in warm months.

nh_cote_boulder_the.blurb: The Cote Boulder is a good-sized block at the foot of Cathedral Ledge near North Conway, one of the boulders gathered below the cliff. It offers eleven problems, a compact set of quality lines. Grades start with an easy V0 and cluster in the V3 to V6 range, with a couple of tougher problems reaching V7 and V8. On the path toward Mordor Wall and Thin Air Face it is easy to spot, off to the right. A handy short session for climbers already visiting the Ledge.
